result:
I’d remove the shame from changing one’s mind.

Not the accountability—just the shame. So that discovering you were wrong felt like becoming larger, not smaller. People could still disagree, still hold deep convictions; but truth would have a better chance against pride.

A remarkable amount of harm persists simply because someone cannot bear to say, “I was wrong.”
